definition: Imitation learning is a paradigm in reinforcement learning, where an agent learns to perform a task by supervised learning from expert demonstrations .
details: It is also called learning from demonstration and apprenticeship learning. It has been applied to underactuated robotics, self-driving cars, quadcopter navigation, helicopter aerobatics, and locomotion.

explainer.lead: Imitation learning trains an agent to perform a task by supervised learning from expert demonstrations. It matters because it lets robots and vehicles acquire skills from recorded expert behavior instead of hand-coded rules.

tiers.eli5: It's learning to do something by watching an expert do it and copying, rather than being told every rule.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers collect expert trajectories and fit a policy that maps states to actions. A key pitfall is distribution shift: the policy drifts into states the expert never visited, where it has no guidance.
tiers.paperLevel: Also called learning from demonstration or apprenticeship learning, it is a reinforcement-learning paradigm using supervised learning on expert demonstrations. Limits include compounding errors under covariate shift and dependence on demonstration quality.

explainer.example: A self-driving model is trained on hours of human driving traces, then must handle situations the human driver never encountered.
